title: Sell Mineral Rights in Fairview, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Fairview, OH
metaDescription: Fairview sits in Belmont County, one of the most active Utica/Point Pleasant counties in Ohio. See what that activity means for your mineral value.
heroLead: Fairview sits in Belmont County, and Belmont has been one of the single most drilled counties in the entire Utica/Point Pleasant play since the early 2010s.
intro: Fairview is a small village in Belmont County, which sits at the structural heart of the Utica/Point Pleasant core and has hosted extensive horizontal drilling for over a decade. Coal mining shaped Belmont County's economy for generations before shale drilling arrived, and much of the land around Fairview passed through coal-company and farm-family hands long before anyone drilled a modern lateral, which means mineral severances here are common and often layered.

sections.heading: Belmont County's role in the core fairway
paragraphs: Belmont County has consistently ranked among Ohio's most active counties for Utica/Point Pleasant production, with operators drilling dense multi-well pads across many of its townships since the play's earliest years. For a mineral owner near Fairview, that history usually means real production data exists somewhere in the county's overall picture, even if your specific tract hasn't been drilled yet.

sections.heading: Coal-era severances layered under Utica-era leases
paragraphs: A lot of Belmont County land carries mineral history in layers: an early coal severance, followed decades later by an oil and gas lease tied to Utica development, sometimes involving different parties entirely for each layer. Sorting out exactly which interest you hold, and whether it's still intact, requires tracing the full chain of title at the Belmont County Recorder's office in St. Clairsville.

faqs.question: Why is Belmont County drilled so heavily?
faqs.answer: It sits in the structural core of the Utica/Point Pleasant fairway, where depth and pressure favor long horizontal laterals, and operators targeted it early once the play was proven in the early 2010s.

faqs.question: Could my land have both coal and oil and gas severances?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's common in Belmont County, where coal was severed generations before shale drilling. Each severance is a separate legal event, so it's worth confirming exactly what your family's mineral reservation actually covers.

faqs.question: How do I know if my interest is inside a currently producing spacing unit?
faqs.answer: The Belmont County Recorder's records will show any lease and related pooling or unitization order for your parcel, and if you're properly identified as an owner on a producing unit, you should be receiving royalty statements.

faqs.question: What if I've received a Dormant Mineral Act notice for my Fairview-area interest?
faqs.answer: Respond within 60 days by filing a claim to preserve with the Belmont County Recorder, or by pointing to an existing lease or royalty record, or a surface owner can complete the abandonment under Ohio law.
